Coated in grey, foul-smelling mud up to her thighs, the 34-year-old mother of four plunges both arms deep into the heavy sediment of a sprawling marsh. Her fingers feel blindly through the silt for the rough, bulbous roots of wild water lilies, known as nyika . Around her, a dozen other women move with deliberate, hushed slowness. No one splashes; no one speaks above a tense whisper.
